items.title: What happens after you buy a house?
items.description: You’ve heard it all before: it’s harder to buy a house.  But, if you do manage to get your foot on the property ladder, things are also more difficult afterwards. The housing crisis has turned into an intergenerational wealth crisis, set to make paying your mortgage in retirement the norm. So how did we get there? And how do we fix it?

items.title: Scientists discover seismic 'stopping phase' in earthquakes

featured_image.name: Japan: KyotoU PEGS away at catching quakes at light speed ...

items.description: Researchers at Kyoto University have discovered a previously unrecognized seismic signal — a distinct "stopping phase" — that marks the moment large earthquakes cease rupturing along a fault. The finding, published Wednesday in the journal Science, could reshape how engineers and seismologists assess earthquake hazards near major fault lines.[1][2]

items.title: Oil surges past $100 as Trump orders Navy to fire on Iranian boats

featured_image.name: US to ‘shoot and kill’ Iranian boats laying mines in Hormuz, Trump says

items.description:
Oil prices surged past $100 a barrel on Thursday as President Donald Trump ordered the U.S. Navy to "shoot and kill" any Iranian boats laying mines in the Strait of Hormuz, deepening a standoff that has disrupted one of the world's most critical shipping lanes for nearly two months.[1][2][3]

Brent crude climbed more than 3% during the session, while West Texas Intermediate also rose sharply, as investors weighed the prospect of prolonged supply disruptions in the Persian Gulf. Asian and European stock markets pulled back from recent highs, with MSCI's global equity index retreating from a record peak.[4][5]

items.title: House panel advances bill cutting US UN funding by 78%

featured_image.name: Trump's FY2027 Budget Is Not Just a Spending Plan - ONEST Network

items.description:
The House Appropriations Subcommittee on National Security, Department of State, and Related Programs advanced a fiscal year 2027 spending bill on Wednesday that would dramatically reduce US funding for international organizations, slashing contributions by roughly 78% and effectively zeroing out US dues for the UN regular budget.

The bill, released on April 22 and marked up on April 23, allocates $310.2 million for Contributions to International Organizations — down from $1.39 billion enacted in fiscal year 2026. It provides $489.5 million for UN peacekeeping activities, a roughly 60% reduction from the $1.23 billion provided in the current fiscal year. The legislation eliminates the International Organizations and Programs account entirely, cutting all voluntary US contributions to agencies including UNICEF, the UN Development Programme, and UN Women.[1][2][3][4]

items.description: President Donald Trump announced on Thursday that the ceasefire between Israel and Lebanon has been extended by three weeks, according to a post on Truth Social, just days before the truce was set to expire on April 26. The extension came as Israeli and Lebanese diplomats held a second round of rare direct talks in Washington.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Nuclear power surges worldwide as Chernobyl's 40th anniversary approaches
items.description: As the world prepares to mark the 40th anniversary of the Chernobyl disaster on April 26, nuclear energy is experiencing a resurgence that would have seemed unthinkable in the decades following the catastrophic 1986 explosion. More than 400 nuclear reactors now operate across 31 countries, with roughly 70 more under construction, and a growing coalition of nations has pledged to triple nuclear capacity by 2050.[1][2]

items.title: Meta to cut 8,000 jobs starting May 20, more layoffs planned for 2026

featured_image.name: Meta lays off employees working on VR in Reality Labs division

items.description:
Meta is preparing to lay off approximately 10% of its global workforce — close to 8,000 employees — beginning May 20, according to Reuters, in what the company views as the first wave of broader cuts planned throughout 2026.[1][2]

Three sources familiar with the plans told Reuters that additional layoffs are expected in the second half of the year, though the timing and scope of those subsequent rounds have not been finalized. The pace of future cuts may depend in part on how the company's artificial intelligence capabilities evolve, the sources said.[3][4][5][2]

items.title: Microsoft offers first voluntary buyout in its 51-year history

featured_image.name: Microsoft is requiring employees return to the office - Yahoo Finance

items.description: Microsoft is offering voluntary retirement buyout packages to a portion of its U.S. workforce, marking the first such program in the company's 51-year history. The one-time initiative, disclosed in an internal memo on Thursday, represents a new approach for the tech giant as it continues reshaping its workforce amid a sweeping industry pivot toward artificial intelligence.
